Why Threads

A test market I did not have to buy

I chose Threads deliberately. My profile, a Taiwanese woman doing an MBA at Stanford and building GTM at a San Francisco AI startup, is exactly the kind of story the Mandarin-speaking Threads audience leans in on. That gives me distribution I did not have to pay for.

I use that reach as a sandbox for Osmo’s messaging. Before a concept goes to the US market, I test it in Mandarin first: the hooks, the framing of what an agentic video editor is for, the objections people raise in the comments. A concept that fails here fails cheaply, in a market that is not the launch market.

The caveat I keep in mind: resonance with a Mandarin audience is a signal, not a proof. I use it to prune concepts and sharpen hooks, then validate the survivors with US creators.

The account has since become an ongoing channel: AI and GTM lessons from inside a startup, plus the personal side of MBA and startup life. If I ask creators to trust my playbook, I should be running it myself.

The holo card, made in Osmo: 372K views for the Jul 30 to Aug 28 window
Threads

What the data says

Numbers first: 384K views and 8.9K interactions in 30 days, 1.5K+ followers, almost all of it from a handful of posts in one week of August. Three things the data taught me:

  • Story earns distribution. The best post, on being a first-generation student who got into Stanford, reached 98.7K views with 89% of them from the algorithmic feed rather than from followers, and drove 501 new follows on its own. Identity-led narrative is what the Threads algorithm carries beyond your audience.
  • Product earns conversation. The Osmo post ↗, a casual reply about AI tools published four days before the public launch, reached 13.2K views but drew 185 replies, a reply rate 14x the viral post, 100+ trial requests, and the company’s first Taiwan user. For messaging tests, replies are the metric, not views: that is where objections and intent show up.
  • Sequencing matters. The career-path post published right after the viral one pulled 40% of its views from profile visits. Story first, product second: the narrative buys the attention that the product content spends.
30-day summary: one week of August did the work
Top posts: story drives reach, product drives replies
The Osmo post: 185 replies on 13.2K views
